Physicist here - The current physical model is that fermions (like electrons) can only have one (well, two if you consider spin) fermion in each energy level. So if you have N electrons, the minimum energy state is when the N lowest energy levels are occupied. If you could in some way use the energy of these electrons, you'd have a HUGE amount of energy (since there are a LOT of electrons out there).

It goes hand in hand with the Fermi energy - which is basically the highest energy level that an electron will occupy if all electrons occupy the lowest possible energy (absolute zero temperature). The Fermi energy is quite large (compared to a single electron's energy, not compared to anything that exists in the "macro" world), which means that the amount of energy "just waiting" in "empty space" is also huge.

Current scientific understanding is that this energy is completely unusable (you can't access it), but science fiction likes to imagine crazy machines that can in fact make use of this near-infinite energy reserve.

When looking at the equations of quantum mechanics, there's two basic types of behavior particles can have:

  • two different particles can be in the same state. We call particles like this Bosons.

  • two different particles can not be in the same state. We call particles like this Fermions.

An example of a Boson is a Photon. You can have many photons at the same state at the same time. This is what a laser does - creates a large number of photons at the same state.

An example of a Fermion is an Electron. You can only have one electron at every state - that's why the electron orbitals of the atom works the way it does - there are multiple energy states (and each energy state has two spin states), and electron fill these states one by one, starting by the lowest energy level. But once that lowest energy level is filled, the next electron has to fill a higher energy level.

This is kinda weird. It sounds "intuitive" how bosons work, and it sounds like Fermions are the "weird" ones, but actually - Bosons are weird. For example, if you have a room filled with electrons - only one (well two) electrons can be "standing still" (have basically 0 energy). All other electrons are moving. They can't stop moving because the "not moving" state is filled! Then there are a very few electrons moving slowly. But since there are a lot of electrons - these are filled too. The "last" electrons actually move very very fast, simply because all "moving slower" states are filled. Weird right?

How fast is "fast"? Well, you might know that temperature is basically "particles are moving around" measurement. So usually at 0 temperature particles are supposed to not move at all. However, electrons even at 0 temperature move at a speed of around one million m/s (2 million mph)! It's a speed you'd expect of particles at 10,000 - 100,000 degrees kelvin! Why? Simply because there are so many of them that all slower speeds are filled. That's fast!

So yea, quantum mechanics is weird.
